ModMetaData.name: Rimrooms - Async Industries
ModMetaData.author: Operator
ModMetaData.description:
Build an organization that investigates, contains, and profits from unstable spaces beyond a machine gate.
Development build 0.10.2-dev: Async Industries facility, company account, staff hiring, facilities overview, procurement, machine operation, saved AI-01 destination, expeditions, investigation, company research, remembered gate addresses with ordinary crossing between connected spaces, the rule that inhabitants stay in the Backrooms unless our own people carry them back, colonists who haul actual goods through a gate as ordinary work in either direction, doorways that can be surveyed and recorded as permanently open ways onward, found deeper in the Backrooms and rarely out in the ordinary world too though never in a door you built yourself, colonists who carry our own downed people and our dead back through a gate to a bed or a grave, colonists who carry real building material through a gate into a real build site, builders who cross a gate to finish a build that already has its material and are never dragged home again, colonists who carry real ingredients through a gate to a workbench whose bill is short of them, researchers who cross a gate to work at a bench on the other side, doctors who cross a gate to treat a patient who stays put and colonists who carry medicine to them, food carried through a gate to people who have none, someone who crosses to feed a patient, and a rescuer who crosses to put a casualty into a bed where they lie instead of carrying them home, cleaning, repair, firefighting, mining, hunting, plant cutting and crop work done across a gate wherever you marked it wanted, wardens, carers and animal handlers who cross for the same reasons, Backrooms spaces that are carved out of solid mineable rock under a ceiling that can never be opened to the sky, and fuel or shells carried to something of yours that has run dry, and settings that let you tune how eagerly colonists cross a gate to work while the game runs, a laboratory gate whose opening lasts long enough to actually work through and grows with research toward being held indefinitely, and a company you name yourself. Cooks, crafters, smiths, tailors and artists who cross a gate to work a bill on the other side, researchers who cross to study the things you have brought back, fishing and the ordinary odd jobs done across a gate too, so every kind of work in the game is now either answered or deliberately left local. A way home that comes up where you marked it. A cutoff switch that closes the lab gate the instant its power is pulled, refused unless the switch genuinely carries that gate's power. And a gate assembly that slowly wears and has to be reconditioned before it runs out, wearing at half rate in a clean sterile room and triple in a filthy one, eight times faster with no power at all, with nobody sent to it until it actually needs it. Anything carried out of a Backrooms coordinate is marked odd, and it never stacks with the ordinary kind, so a thousand odd cotton is a thing you went and fetched rather than a thing you grew. Buyers turn up wanting odd goods and paying well over the ordinary rate, and they only ever ask for things a space you have actually opened really held. Original Backrooms menu backgrounds show the mod title and loaded version beside the native version information. Every laboratory gate keeps its own list of everywhere it has connected to, which you can rename, pin, remove and clear. Opening a connection is no longer a button: the operator brings the gate up at the console over time, the console shows the progress, and leaving it unattended loses the charge. A route your crew has run before comes up faster than one they have never taken. A gate you have designated is a plainly blue door with a blue glow around it, so you can tell one from an ordinary door at a glance. The last custom gate machine, control console, cutoff switch and generator are gone: a gate is an ordinary door you designate, its controls are an ordinary comms console and machining table, and its power comes off your own grid like everything else. The unused site lamp, climate unit, analysis bench and carpet went with them. A gate can be wider than one cell. An ordinary door gives you a one-wide gate, and the game's own ornate door gives you a two-wide one with no other mods at all; Doors Expanded adds three-wide and the big two-by-three blast door if you run it. A wider gate is more machine to power and takes longer to bring up, and it cannot be resized while it is working. Everything this mod adds that you can look at now tells you what it is: the facilities overview explains what each kind of room is for and what goes wrong without it, and the procurement list says what each thing is actually good for rather than just its price. Your animals can walk through a gate now, and how big a creature fits depends on how wide the gate is: an ordinary doorway passes people and working animals, a two-wide one passes pack animals like muffalo and dromedaries, and three wide or more passes anything at all. In the worst coordinates, what lives there no longer holds its ground. It follows your crew, through room after room, all the way to the doorway you came in by. In every quieter space it still gives you a warning and lets you back away, which is what makes the deep ones mean something. And once your gate is advanced enough, in the worst coordinates, a thing that reaches the doorway behind your crew can step through it into the facility, where it behaves like anything else that gets inside. Only one per opening, only if it fits through the gate, and never from a quiet space. Closing the connection before it arrives is what stops it, which finally makes the emergency cutoff a decision rather than a formality. Some places down there are bigger than a room. Runs of two to four connected rooms are furnished as one thing, so you find a laboratory wing rather than a room with a bench in it, a dormitory block rather than a stray bed. Deeper in they are still wrong in all the usual ways, which is worse than a jumble because there is finally something recognisable for the wrongness to happen to. The return beacon is gone. Your gate remembers every address it has dialled and the way back is saved with the space itself, so carrying a beacon to find your own door stopped being a job some time ago. Everything the mod shows you now uses one set of words: the gate is the machine in your wall, the connection is the live link it holds open, and the threshold is the doorway you arrive at on the far side. Gameplay acceptance is pending; this is not a finished campaign release.
Designed for RimWorld 1.6. No DLC, no Harmony and no other mod is required by this package: every game definition it uses is base Core, audited and listed in the project's dependency record. Optional mods are used through public interfaces when present and their absence is never a failure path. Existing-game-content replacement, the full procedural campaign, further scenarios, RimWorld Together cooperation and optional integrations remain under development. This source checkpoint still contains historical custom gameplay objects being replaced under the project's existing-content policy.
Author: Operator.
